So the defect is missing tier words on true claims, which a tier-only fix-up repairs without touching a boundary; sending 12 of W1's 13 rows untiered to two blind primaries would spend both lanes on a defect already measured. Why layer names and not file names: item 7 says 'EXTRACTED with its file' and 'MEASURED with its script', but CWO-DAN-04 (E1, binding) requires zero file stems and zero .py names in prose fields. I do not amend CWO-DAN-04. I say in words that this order satisfies item 7 by a layer name in the row and the file or scan in the change record, which is weaker than the letter of item 7; it follows the form 61 rows already use (MEASURED by work\r2.py: '(EXTRACTED, device inventory)' 12 times, '(EXTRACTED, OSHB mark layer)' 9, '(MEASURED over the OSHB mark layer)' 3) and it goes to Fable's end review. Why observed_substrate_signals is out of scope: MEASURED by work\r2.py, entries of that field carry a tier word in W3 only (10 of 39) and in no other part (0 of 301); tiering it in 15 rows would not make the corpus consistent, and the field is a list of substrate tokens whose source is its own name. Why boundary_evidence_refs is out of scope: no entry in any of the 75 rows carries a tier word (MEASURED, same script); each entry names its witness by its 'oshb:' or 'web:' prefix, and W1 mark refs already say 'single-witness WLC paragraph mark'. Both exclusions are stated, not hidden, and go to the end review. No ruling here adjudicates a divided reading. W1-009 and W1-010 touch seam region (o) and W2-007 seam (d); their spans, confidence grades and end-review routing (E2 S1-09-ROUTING) are unchanged.

orders.order: TIER-ONLY RULE. In each row and field in scope the author inserts provenance annotations and does nothing else. (a) Grammar: every insertion is one string matching the regex G =  \((?:(?:EXTRACTED|MEASURED), (?:OSHB/WLC|WEB|OSHB mark layer|device inventory|language-zone layer|WEB/MT crosswalk)(?: and (?:OSHB/WLC|WEB|OSHB mark layer|device inventory|language-zone layer|WEB/MT crosswalk))?|INFERRED|REPORTED|ASSUMED|UNAVAILABLE)\) (a leading space, then one parenthesis). No other character of the field changes: no word, verse reference, quotation, punctuation mark or space is added, removed or moved. (b) Placement: directly before the punctuation mark that ends the sentence or clause the annotation covers, or at the very end of the field. (c) Coverage: every sentence that states a fact about a witness (a mark, a word or formula at a verse, a ketiv/qere or editorial-note site, a count, the language of a verse or span) or that draws a conclusion (one episode, a closed speech act, a seam is weak, a rival is rejected because ...) carries at least one annotation; each field in scope holds at least one. A bare pointer to the strategy (D1, D4, D5, D6, D7, guard (d), region (a), (b), (h), (o)) is not a claim about the text and takes no annotation of its own. (d) Truth: EXTRACTED is written only where the author opened the pinned file of the named layer and found the claim in its bytes, and the change record cites that file and the verse or key. The layer names stand for pinned files: 'OSHB/WLC' = Dan_oshb.txt; 'WEB' = Dan_web_clean.txt; 'OSHB mark layer' = pmarks_Dan.json (its marks, paseq, kq and note keys); 'device inventory' = dan_device_inventory.json; 'language-zone layer' = dan_language_zones.json; 'WEB/MT crosswalk' = web_mt_offset_map.json. A layer may be named only if its file is pinned in the author's brief. The file stem is never written in the row (CWO-DAN-04 stays at zero hits); it is written in the change record. MEASURED is written only for a negative, range or count claim (for example 'no mark in 1:1-1:20', 'No mark at this seam', 'No K/Q note in 8:15-8:18', 'Unmarked stretch') and only where the author ran a scan of the named layer's pinned file in the author's own work directory; the change record carries the scan's code and its output. Without such a scan the claim is INFERRED. A conclusion, a reading of structure or a weighing is INFERRED. A divided reading or a statement of what others hold is REPORTED and is not adjudicated. The author never raises a tier above what the bytes support. (e) Never delete and never correct. A claim the author cannot support from the pinned bytes is annotated (INFERRED). A claim the author finds CONTRADICTED by the pinned bytes is left exactly as it stands, gets no annotation, and is listed in the author's final message with the bytes; it returns to the controlling agent. (f) Unchanged: span, confidence, unit_type, boundary_evidence_refs, strong_or_hebrew_tags_used, observed_substrate_signals, literature_type_guess and every other field of the row; every other row. (g) Records: one change record per insertion or replacement, carrying row, field, entry index (null for a string field; an integer for a list field), a 'before' text that occurs exactly once in that field, and the 'after' text. Output files have LF line endings and no CR byte.

rulings.decision: No S3 review. The orchestrator applies FIXUP-3 and then measures conditions C1 through C11 (written in full in gate.primaries_conditions) and installs them by receipt. The proposal's six checks are kept and made exact; added are the regex that defines an allowed insertion, proof that MEASURED words have scans behind them, byte-for-byte replay of the change records, the seven-word repeat member, an unchanged bare-reference count, and a rule for which new flags the orchestrator may dispose alone. Any failed condition comes back to the controlling agent. CWO-DAN-01 through CWO-DAN-04 remain binding exactly as E1 wrote them; none is amended here and no new corpus-wide order is made.
rulings.reason: The S2-N2 edits are three exact spans. The S2-N1 edits are confined by grammar: if deleting the insertions gives back the old text, no claim, boundary or quotation changed, and that is a script's job, not a reader's. What no script here proves is whether each added tier word is TRUE. I do not hide that: it is the residual risk of having no S3. It is carried by three things: C5 for MEASURED and for the presence of an EXTRACTED citation, the two blind primaries who read all 75 rows and are ordered to test the added tiers in the 15 rows, and Fable's end review. A third same-family review lane would add one more voice of the same weights (OW-19, OW-25), which is a poor trade against a scripted check plus two blind lanes. Risks I looked for in the bytes: a repeated annotation could trip the seven-word repeat member, though an annotation is short and sits between differing words, so C6 names that member; the register member already flagged 'the device inventory' once (E2, T-REG-FX2-001, tool_false_positive), so new flags of that kind are expected and C9 says who may dispose them; an insertion has no digit, so it cannot add a verse reference (C7 holds the bare-reference count fixed).

primaries_conditions: C1 (base and form): the FIXUP-3 applied rows file is built from SP\Dan\fixup\draft_rows_fixup2_applied.jsonl with sha256 d731d8559d100caace5152abb799b7af6a43d2f598eb6f8fb6bca49b78b893e5; it has 75 rows, the same decision_id order, the same key order in every row, and zero CR bytes.

Every other value in all 75 rows is byte-identical.

C3 (tier-only): for each changed field, take the new text, turn the three S2-N2 replacements back (each 'after' span of S2-N2 restored to its 'before' span, in W1-004.device_notes, W1-009.device_notes and W1-010.strongest_rejected_alternative only), delete every match of the regex G =  \((?:(?:EXTRACTED|MEASURED), (?:OSHB/WLC|WEB|OSHB mark layer|device inventory|language-zone layer|WEB/MT crosswalk)(?: and (?:OSHB/WLC|WEB|OSHB mark layer|device inventory|language-zone layer|WEB/MT crosswalk))?|INFERRED|REPORTED|ASSUMED|UNAVAILABLE)\), and the result equals the old text exactly. The count of G matches deleted equals the count of insertion change records.

C4 (coverage): each of the 44 ordered (row, field) pairs contains at least one of the words MEASURED, EXTRACTED, REPORTED, INFERRED, ASSUMED, UNAVAILABLE; a whole-row scan of all 75 rows finds zero rows without a tier word; the regex \bFable\b matches in zero string values of any row.

C5 (MEASURED backed): every inserted annotation beginning '(MEASURED' has a change record that carries scan code and scan output; the orchestrator re-runs each scan on the pinned file and gets the same output. Every inserted '(EXTRACTED' has a change record naming a pinned file and a verse or key.
C6 (suite): on the applied file the suite reports hard_status GREEN with no dead member, the seven-word repeat member GREEN, and tiling GREEN at 357 of 357 verses and 75 decisions.

C7 (corpus-wide orders, unamended): CWO-DAN-01, CWO-DAN-02 and CWO-DAN-04 each return zero hits; CWO-DAN-03 returns zero zone hits and the same bare-reference count as before FIXUP-3 (S2 REPORTED 124); each sweep reports rows swept 75 and the count of strings swept.

C8 (records replay): every change record has row, field, entry index and a 'before' that occurs exactly once in the field at the moment it is applied; applying the records in order to the base file reproduces the applied file byte for byte (equal sha256).

C9 (triage): the flag list on the applied file is diffed against the 137 flags before. A flag whose flagged text is byte-identical to a flag already disposed keeps that disposition. A new flag whose flagged span lies wholly inside an inserted G match may be disposed tool_false_positive by the orchestrator on the precedent of E2 TRIAGE-CLASSES (T-REG-FX2-001). Any other new flag returns to the controlling agent. Zero flags are left without a disposition.
C10 (no refusals): no FIXUP-3 author's final message lists a claim contradicted by the bytes; if one does, it returns to the controlling agent before any launch.

C11 (receipt and briefs): C1 through C10, each with its script name, its output and the sha256 of the applied file, are installed by receipt; the primaries' briefs carry the S2-N5-COVERAGE note, the E3-N1-FIELDS list and the order to test the truth of every tier word in the 15 FIXUP-3 rows.
